original_question: For the focusing nonlinear Schrodinger equation on the half-line, i u_t = u_{xx} + 2 |u|^2 u for x >= 0 and t >= 0, with prescribed initial data u(x,0) = f(x) and oscillatory boundary forcing u(0,t) = e^{i w t}, can one compute the long-time asymptotic behavior of the solution u(x,t) for general real driving frequency w?
target_in_paper: Problem 5 (initial boundary value problems for integrable systems (IBVP)): the paper’s 'particular stand out open problem' asking for the long-time behavior, as t -> infinity, of the solution of the half-line focusing NLS i u_t = u_xx + 2|u|^2 u with u(x,0)=f(x) for x>=0 and u(0,t)=e^{iwt} for t>=0, where w is real (Problem 5, p. 12).
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s main target very closely: it identifies the focusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the half-line, the initial datum u(x,0)=f(x), the oscillatory Dirichlet boundary forcing u(0,t)=e^{iwt}, the parameter w in R, and the objective of determining the long-time behavior as t -> infinity. This is exactly the stand-out open problem singled out in Problem 5 (Problem 5, p. 12).
missing_details: The paper frames this as a specific open problem inside Problem 5 on initial-boundary value problems for integrable systems, not as a general theorem request (Problem 5, p. 12).

The nearby context explains the main analytical obstruction: in Fokas’ unified-transform approach, the half-line NLS problem is generally overdetermined, since one typically also needs the Neumann trace u_x(0,t) in addition to u(x,0)=f(x) and u(0,t)=g(t); the difficulty here is precisely that no a priori formula for u_x(0,t) is available in general (Problem 5, p. 12).
The paper states the parameter precisely as w in R and asks for the asymptotic behavior of the resulting solution u(x,t) as t -> infinity for that boundary drive (Problem 5, p. 12).

The paper notes that only partial results are known in the high-frequency regime w -> infinity, citing Fokas-Lenells [57]; the unresolved problem is the full real-frequency case, not just large w (Problem 5, p. 12).

The continuation of the discussion records the intended qualitative expectation: by analogy with a periodically driven Toda lattice, one expects richer propagating structures as w decreases, potentially including k-gap periodic NLS waves emerging from the boundary driver e^{iwt} as w decreases toward 0 (Problem 5, p. 13).

The paper does not specify a precise regularity or decay class for f in this problem statement; it simply says the initial data are given, so a faithful stand-alone formulation should avoid inventing extra hypotheses and only assume that the half-line IBVP is well posed for the chosen f (Problem 5, p. 12).
refined_question: For the half-line initial-boundary value problem for the focusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation i u_t = u_xx + 2|u|^2 u on x>=0, t>=0, with prescribed initial data u(x,0)=f(x) for x>=0 and Dirichlet boundary forcing u(0,t)=e^{iwt} for t>=0, where w is any real number and no a priori expression for the Neumann trace u_x(0,t) is assumed, determine the asymptotic behavior of the solution u(x,t) as t -> infinity.
justification: Although your instructions mention Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, and Theorem 1.3, this draft clearly targets a different part of the paper: Problem 5. Deift explicitly calls this focusing-NLS half-line IBVP with boundary data e^{iwt} a 'particular stand out open problem' and asks for the long-time behavior of its solution (Problem 5, p. 12). The surrounding discussion also explains why this formulation should mention the absence of an a priori Neumann datum u_x(0,t): in the general half-line NLS problem, Fokas’ method is overdetermined unless that extra boundary value is known or can be recovered in a special integrable case (Problem 5, p. 12). I kept the reformulation narrow by not broadening to other boundary conditions or other NLS variants, and by not hard-wiring low-frequency finite-gap behavior into the main question; the paper presents that only as a heuristic expectation by analogy with the driven Toda lattice, not as an equivalent formal statement (Problem 5, p. 13).
